$comment: Single owner for: which backend capabilities the dashboard e2e specs require, and
which environment starts a backend that has them.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS (anchored 2026-08-06).
A dashboard e2e spec declares its backend precondition in its own fixture, and the
CI job that runs it declares the backend environment in its own `run:` block. Nothing
connected the two, so they drifted, twice, in a single nightly run:
- nightly.yml 'Dashboard all tests' starts a plain standalone backend and then runs
`npm run test:pages`, which is `playwright test --project=e2e-ui` with NO path
filter and therefore includes tests/e2e-ui/full/. cluster_peers.spec.ts threw
'Cluster peer specs require a replication-enabled HA backend' in run 31072375322.
- ci.yml 'Dashboard full e2e tests' starts a replication-enabled backend but omits
FLAPJACK_AI_ALLOW_LOCAL_URLS, so vector-settings.spec.ts failed three times in
prod CI run 31096601354 with 'rest embedder URL private or local destination
`127.0.0.1` is not allowed'.
Both specs were correct and both passed their authoring lane's own proof, because
that lane started a backend that satisfied them. The defect is that the workflow's
backend and the spec's precondition had no shared owner.
WHY THE ENVIRONMENT MUST BE ON THE BACKEND STARTUP STEP, NOT THE TEST STEP.
This is the trap that makes the bug non-obvious. scripts/playwright-webserver.mjs
starts a correctly-configured backend via spawnBackendServer — but startPlaywrightServers
passes allowReuse: true for the backend, so when a workflow has already started one on
the target port, Playwright REUSES it and spawnBackendServer never runs. Environment
declared on the Playwright step therefore cannot reach the process under test. Only the
step that launches the binary can satisfy these requirements.
HOW TO ADD A REQUIREMENT.
Add an entry below naming the env, the specs that need it, and the exact symptom when
it is missing. engine/tests/test_dashboard_e2e_backend_contract.py then fails every
workflow job whose spec selection includes one of those specs without that env, and
fails spawnBackendServer if it does not provide the union of all of them.
BASE vs PER-SPEC, AND WHY GETTING THIS WRONG IS INVISIBLE (anchored 2026-08-07).
Set "base": true when assertBackendReadiness itself enforces the requirement, i.e.
the harness refuses the backend at webServer startup before any spec runs. Leave it
unset when only named specs need it at request time. The distinction is load-bearing
because a per-spec requirement is checked only against a job's spec SELECTION, so a
job that selects none of the named specs passes this gate and then dies at startup
anyway. That is exactly what happened: ci.yml's dashboard-pages and
dashboard-integration jobs carried neither replication nor ai_local_outbound, this
gate exited 0, and staging run 31213083385 failed both jobs with 'refused the
dashboard local-URL embedder probe' before a single spec executed. The rule to keep:
a static contract that guarantees a runtime assertion must be at least as strict as
that assertion, and assertBackendReadiness is the assertion here.

requirements.why_base: assertBackendReadiness calls assertReplicationEnabled unconditionally for every backend it accepts or spawns, so this is required regardless of which specs a job selects. It is NOT only cluster_peers.spec.ts's requirement, even though that spec is the reason the values were chosen.
requirements.why: Runtime HA membership (ROADMAP HA-MEMBERSHIP-UI) is a real product surface. Its specs drive add/remove peer mutations through /internal/cluster/*, which the server only registers when replication is configured. No peers are configured — a single node with a replication identity is enough for the membership UI to be exercised, and ci.yml's dashboard-full-e2e job has run 400+ specs in exactly this configuration since 2026-08-03.
requirements.symptom_if_missing: Cluster peer specs require a replication-enabled HA backend, but the target reports standalone mode

requirements.why_base: assertBackendReadiness calls probeLocalOutboundOptIn for every backend it accepts or spawns (skipped only under the P20_TEXT_ONLY_NEGATIVE_CONTROL negative control), so this is required regardless of which specs a job selects. Modelling it as vector-settings.spec.ts's private requirement is what let ci.yml's dashboard-pages and dashboard-integration jobs ship without it: the guard passed and the harness refused anyway.
requirements.why: vector-settings.spec.ts stands up a deterministic embedder on 127.0.0.1 and registers it as a `rest` source. engine/src/security.rs::allow_local_outbound_urls reads FLAPJACK_AI_ALLOW_LOCAL_URLS and outbound_ip_block_reason refuses a private or loopback destination when it is absent. That refusal is a deliberate fail-closed SSRF control with a documented operator opt-in for exactly this local-AI case; the fix is to set the opt-in in the harness, NEVER to weaken security.rs.
requirements.symptom_if_missing: rest embedder URL private or local destination `127.0.0.1` is not allowed

requirements.why: The Meilisearch and Typesense provider migration happy-path specs use digest-pinned loopback source fixtures. Once the release fallback is available, those submit paths require the preview loopback opt-ins at backend process start; setting them on the Playwright step is too late when a backend is already listening and reused.
requirements.symptom_if_missing: Meilisearch Cloud endpoint is not allowed / Typesense Cloud endpoint is not allowed

requirements.why: The Meilisearch refusal spec proves the console adds operator guidance when the backend rejects a loopback source. That proof is only meaningful when FJ_ENABLE_MEILISEARCH_PREVIEW_LOOPBACK is absent from the backend process start environment. Run it through `npm run test:e2e-ui:migrate-meilisearch-refusal`, which selects only the refusal project and narrows PLAYWRIGHT_BACKEND_CONTRACT_IDS to the non-preview base requirements.
requirements.symptom_if_missing: The refusal case cannot receive `Meilisearch Cloud endpoint is not allowed` if the backend was started with FJ_ENABLE_MEILISEARCH_PREVIEW_LOOPBACK=1

$comment: Resolved from engine/dashboard/package.json at gate time rather than restated here.
This map only records which scripts are dashboard Playwright entry points; the gate
reads the actual script body to learn which paths it selects, so a script that gains
or loses a path filter cannot silently escape the contract.
